claude_defect_list.issue: Rival 1 (deterministic-only) overlaps the H0 falsifier band: both predict CV<0.1/0.05 from seed variance, so the same seed-CV measurement cannot separate 'deterministic simulator' from 'no biological noise' — they are confounded, not discriminated.

If the simulator is deterministic (Rival 1), the falsifier's H1-refute branch (CV<0.1) will always fire regardless of biology, so H1 cannot survive even in a correct-but-deterministic engine — the test measures the simulator, not the hypothesis.
The decision rule leaves CV in [0.1,0.3) as a dead zone that neither rejects H0 nor H1; no decision is specified for this interval, so the falsifier can be inconclusive.

Intrinsic-vs-extrinsic noise is classically separable only via dual-reporter (two-color) decomposition; a single-gene CV plus one correlation cannot measure 'intrinsic noise' as claimed, exceeding what this observable supports.

Assumes different seeds are independent isogenic replicates and that measurement/numerical noise CV<<0.1, but provides no in-design verification (e.g., repeat-run or deterministic-baseline check) establishing this.
'Steady-state at generation 3' is asserted but no stationarity criterion is given to confirm transients have decayed, making the sampling point unverifiable.

The relA-knockout control's prediction (CV remains ≥ 0.3) is not tied to any decision rule that would change the conclusion if violated, so it does not actually discriminate the ppGpp-amplification rival.
acrB is assumed to be mid-abundance (~10–100 mRNA/cell) and constitutive, but this is asserted without verification; if acrB is low-copy/bursty or regulated, the CV≥0.3 threshold is uncalibrated.

The extrinsic-noise rival is nullified by the auxiliary that the model 'does not simulate spatial microenvironments or extrinsic noise sources' — by design extrinsic noise is absent, so the test cannot ever favor the rival and is not discriminating.

The deterministic-chaos rival admits that each seed is a distinct noise realization and that distinguishing chaos from noise is 'beyond this model's scope' — changing seed trivially changes output, so H1 is supported by construction, not by evidence.

The CV ranges conflict: claim/predicted effect say CV 0.15–0.40 (median ≈0.20) per gene, yet H1 and the decision rule only require CV>0.10, so a gene with CV=0.12 would satisfy H1 while refuting the stated predicted effect.
The falsifier channel fixes protein[acrB] but the decision rule evaluates a panel of ≥10 genes; the single-channel falsifier does not operationalize the panel-level claim actually being tested.

No specified gene panel list or expression-tier assignment is given despite the decision rule requiring '≥10 representative genes spanning low/medium/high expression'; which genes and their tiers are left undefined.

The mass-normalization rival requires per-cell cell_mass/protein_mass at the sampling point, but the operational defs measure protein counts across seeds without establishing that paired per-cell mass observables are available.

Given the auxiliary that all observed CV is attributed to intrinsic stochasticity by design and seeds inject noise, a nonzero CV>0.10 is essentially guaranteed by the simulator construction, making H1 near-unfalsifiable in practice.
'Representative genes' and 'representative range of expression levels and regulatory architectures' are asserted but not defined by any measurable selection criterion.

Two of the three candidate designs (ppgpp_conc, rrna_operon_knockout) are perturbations irrelevant to the isogenic-same-environment question and do not feed any stated decision rule or rival discrimination.

The extrinsic-noise rival relies on ribosome_conc CV<0.10 for intrinsic noise, but the auxiliary assumption already asserts high-copy buffering suppresses ribosome CV regardless of mechanism, so the comparison cannot cleanly separate intrinsic from extrinsic.
Falsifier rejects H1 at CV<0.10 while H0 is defined as CV≤0.05 and the claim/prediction use CV≥0.15; the 0.10–0.15 band is an undecided no-man's-land left unassigned.

Treating each seed as 'one isogenic cell' assumes the simulator models single cells rather than population-averaged ODEs; if it is a bulk/average model, inter-seed CV measures something other than cell-to-cell biological heterogeneity.

The assumption admits that a deterministic-only engine will 'trivially reject H1 (a scope limitation),' meaning the falsifier may fail for engine reasons unrelated to the biological claim, confounding rejection.

The rpoS-knockout rival predicts acrB CV drops to <0.10 if RpoS-driven, but acrB is stated to be RpoS-independent, so there is no mechanistic reason its CV would fall under rpoS knockout—both hypotheses predict unchanged CV, giving no discrimination.

ppgpp_conc clamp with factor=2.0 doubles ppGpp rather than fixing/clamping it; a scaled-but-still-fluctuating level does not 'eliminate variance,' so the design does not implement the stated clamp test.
Predicted effect claims '~2–3 fold range between low and high expressors' but CV≥0.15 does not entail a 2–3 fold range, making the stated magnitude unmeasured and inconsistent with the threshold.
Steady-state at generation 8 is assumed without specifying how transient decay is verified; no convergence check is defined, so residual initialization variance could masquerade as expression noise.

H1 requires CV≥0.15 in 'at least one of ten channels' — with 10 correlated mass/growth observables this threshold is nearly guaranteed to be met by some channel, so the falsifier's arm (a) almost cannot trigger.
H1 text says heterogeneity appears 'across all ten measured channels' but the claim/threshold only requires CV≥0.15 in at least one channel; 'all ten' vs 'at least one' are inconsistent.

Persistence threshold is stated inconsistently: H1 and predicted_effect use CV≥0.12 under clamp/KO, but the falsifier refutes only if CV<0.08, leaving the 0.08–0.12 gap undefined (neither confirms nor refutes).

The ppGpp-clamp design (multiplier=1.0) sets ppGpp to its mean but the auxiliary assumption that this 'eliminates fluctuations without shifting the mean' is untested; if the clamp merely rescales rather than freezes fluctuations, clamp vs intrinsic-noise rivals are not distinguished.

Whether the simulator actually implements single-cell stochasticity (Gillespie/partition noise) is listed as an assumption but is the load-bearing premise; if the sim is deterministic per-seed-independent, the entire design collapses and this is not verified.

Claim distinguishes 'intrinsic stochastic gene expression' (partition noise, transcriptional bursting) from stringent-response fluctuations, but the CV-across-seeds instrument cannot separate intrinsic from extrinsic noise or identify bursting as the mechanism.

The measurement-noise rival predicts CV<0.05 everywhere, but 'measurement noise negligible' is asserted by assumption rather than measured via replicate/technical-noise controls, so the rival cannot be empirically ruled out.

'Per-seed readouts capture single-cell snapshots rather than population averages' is assumed but unverified; if channels are population averages, CV across seeds does not measure cell-to-cell variability as claimed.
The decision rule leaves a dead zone (0.10≤0.15 in wildtype) where neither H1 confirm nor refutation arm (a) applies, so some outcomes yield no verdict.
The broad question 'do identical cells behave differently?' is reduced to CV in ten specific mass/translation observables at generation 3, excluding spatial, temporal, and behavioral phenotypes.

Claim/H1 set the threshold at CV ≥ 0.15, but the falsifier rejects H1 only if CV < 0.10, so a CV between 0.10 and 0.15 both fails the stated claim yet does not refute H1 — the gating threshold contradicts the hypothesis threshold.

The steady-state construct defines 'steady' as CV(gen8)-CV(gen4) < 0.03, but the falsifier uses >0.05 as the rejection bound, leaving a 0.03–0.05 inconsistency band where the hypothesis is neither steady nor refuted.

H1 specifies independence as Pearson |r| < 0.5, but the falsifier and rival use |r| > 0.7 as the refutation/extrinsic bound, so |r| in 0.5–0.7 violates H1 yet neither refutes it nor confirms the rival.
The void clause (CV < 0.02 ⇒ deterministic, test void) lets a null result escape as 'void' rather than a refutation, so the falsifier cannot fail against a low-variance outcome.

The ppGpp clamp rival states CV ≥ 0.15 under the clamp 'rules out' ppGpp extrinsic noise, but ribosome-driven extrinsic noise is uncontrolled, so a high CV cannot distinguish intrinsic noise from non-ppGpp extrinsic sources.

The transient/cell-cycle rival uses the same CV(gen8)-CV(gen4) metric as the steady-state def; a monotonic CV decrease could reflect either transient relaxation or cell-cycle desynchronization — the test does not separate these two rival mechanisms.

The correlation falsifier assumes ribosome_conc CV across seeds is large enough to detect correlation; if extrinsic/ribosome variance is tiny, |r| is undefined/uninformative and low |r| trivially 'confirms' intrinsic noise.

No specification of how many cells per seed are sampled or whether CV is over seeds (one lineage each) vs. over a population — single-cell CV vs. seed-mean CV conflation is left unstated and critical to the measured quantity.

'Global physiological fluctuations' is operationalized only via ribosome_conc (and ppGpp), so 'independent of global physiological fluctuations' is not generally measurable — low correlation with one channel does not establish independence from global state.

The question asks about genes generally, but the test examines a single gene (acrB) at moderate copy number, so a single-gene result cannot answer whether isogenic cells express 'the same gene' identically across genes.

Rival 2 (extrinsic vs intrinsic) interprets CV>=0.15 in the doubled-copy design as supporting extrinsic, but H1's own prediction expects substantial intrinsic noise; the design cannot cleanly separate because it lacks the two-reporter (same-cell) construct standard for intrinsic/extrinsic decomposition.

The extrinsic-factors rival relies on across-seed CV of a doubled-copy strain, but intrinsic/extrinsic decomposition requires two distinguishable copies measured in the SAME cell; across-seed CV conflates both sources and cannot discriminate.

Rival 1 (numerical noise) is only excluded if fixed_seed mode exists; the auxiliary assumptions concede that if fixed_seed is unsupported the rival 'must be accepted', so the design does not actually discriminate it.

The '2 of 3 genes' threshold combined with wide CV>=0.15-0.20 targets and a generous +0.10 margin makes the falsifier easy to satisfy; no pre-registered power analysis shows 30 seeds can detect failure to exceed Poisson.

The protocol depends on a 'fixed_seed' parameter and verified Gillespie/tau-leaping stochasticity, but the auxiliaries admit the simulator may not support fixed_seed, leaving a core control possibly unexecutable.
Assumes 30 seeds yield a stable CV estimate, but CV sampling error at n=30 can be ~13%, comparable to the 0.10 margin, and no confidence interval or estimator-bias correction is specified.

Poisson baseline 1/sqrtN assumes protein counts are themselves Poisson, but protein noise reflects upstream mRNA bursting and dilution/partitioning; the correct null baseline for protein CV is not justified.
The three gene_knockout designs are listed as controls but only confirm readout specificity (zero expression); they do not discriminate among any of the stated rival hypotheses.
'Representative set of genes' is claimed from only three hand-picked genes with no criteria for representativeness, so a general claim about all genes cannot be measured by this sample.

The question asks whether identical cells express 'the same gene' at the same level, but measuring CV across independent seeds at division of generation 3 conflates cell-to-cell variation with cell-cycle-timing and partitioning effects rather than isolating same-gene expression differences.

predicted_effect requires N~100-1000 giving CV>=0.15-0.20, but auxiliary assumptions list rpoB as high-copy N~400-1000 with CV~0.03-0.05 near Poisson, so rpoB cannot simultaneously meet the 2-of-3 threshold and the high-copy-deterministic expectation.

Claim/H1/predicted_effect use thresholds CV_gr>=0.30, F_gr>=20%, CV_rib>=0.25, F_rib>=15%, but the falsifier rejects H1 only if CV_gr<0.15 OR F_gr<0.10 (etc.), leaving a wide dead zone (e.g. CV_gr=0.20) where neither H1 nor H0 is confirmed yet the claim is not refuted.

The OR-within-AND decision rule makes refutation extremely hard: a single high observable (either CV OR F above the low cutoff, on either channel) prevents rejection, so the falsifier almost never triggers against a stochastic simulator that trivially yields CV>0.

The ppGpp-clamp rival is self-defeating: the hypothesis itself admits 'the simulator may not model ppGpp noise explicitly,' so observing no CV reduction cannot distinguish the environmental-artifact rival from H1.

The micro-fluctuation rival conflates measurement/environmental noise with intrinsic noise, but both candidate designs are identical static-basal multi-seed runs; nothing isolates an environmental-noise source, so the rival cannot be discriminated by the proposed designs.
The chaos rival's distinguishing test (repeated runs of the identical seed) is explicitly stated to be unsupported by the instrument, so this rival is not actually testable within the design.

Treats CV across independent seeds as equivalent to single-cell phenotypic heterogeneity within one clonal population, but seed-to-seed variance of whole-run summaries need not equal cell-to-cell heterogeneity in a growing population; this mapping is assumed, not justified.

'2-fold deviation' is operationalized as |x-median|/median>=1.0, which only captures upward 2-fold (ratio>=2) and conflates it with a downward deviation that can never reach 1.0 (min possible is 1.0 at x=0), biasing F_gr/F_rib asymmetrically.

The broad question 'do genetically identical cells behave differently?' is narrowed to just two observables (growth_rate, ribosome_conc) at a single timepoint (generation 3), which the auxiliaries merely assert is 'sufficient breadth' without justification.
Choice of generation 3 as the timepoint where transients have decayed but drift/selection have not set in is asserted without any supporting criterion or sensitivity analysis.

Rival 1 (translation burst) relies on protein/mRNA ratio and CAI/codon effects, but auxiliary assumption 6 concedes codon/ribosome details are averaged or absent, so the proposed discriminating test cannot actually run.

Rival 2 requires distinguishing burst frequency vs size and a ppGpp clamp, but auxiliary assumption 5 states the model doesn't track burst frequency/size separately and the single candidate design has no ppgpp_conc clamp, so the test is not instantiated.
The ppGpp clamp (2x basal) and stringent-vs-constitutive promoter comparison are named for Rival 2 but absent from candidate_designs (only one wildtype/basal run), so they cannot be executed.
Rival 3's intrinsic/extrinsic variance partitioning requires a dual-reporter or two-gene decomposition scheme that the summary CV-across-seeds readout does not provide.

Decision rule has overlapping/under-specified gaps: slopes in (-0.3, -0.2] and R2 in [0.3,0.6) with CI excluding both 0 and -0.5 yield neither H0 nor H1 rejection, leaving indeterminate outcomes rather than a clean falsification.
H0 is defined as R2 < 0.3 but the reject-H0 condition requires R2 >= 0.6 and slope CI in [-0.7,-0.3]; outcomes between these thresholds satisfy neither rejection, contradicting the stated dichotomy.

The -0.5 shot-noise scaling assumes protein CV is driven by mRNA Poisson noise with comparable per-gene mRNA/protein half-lives; auxiliary notes flag that uniform half-lives would confound but never verify the model's gene-specific rates.

Question asks what makes any gene noisier; the test uses only 5 named genes, insufficient to robustly estimate a slope/R2 and excluding whole regulatory classes, so conclusions can't generalize to 'one gene vs another'.

Falsifier requires >=5 genes with mean_mRNA spanning >=1 order of magnitude, but whether the fixed panel actually achieves this range is only assumed (aux assumption 4), not established; if range collapses the regression is uninformative.

'mRNA burst size' is the central causal construct but is operationalized only as mean mRNA copy number, which conflates burst size, burst frequency, and degradation and cannot isolate burst size as claimed.

Translation-rate proxy protein/mRNA is mathematically coupled to the CV_protein and mRNA_mean being correlated; partialling on a ratio built from the same variables induces spurious structure, undermining the 'independent of translation rate' claim.

The translational-bursting rival predicts |r_partial(CV,trans|mRNA)|>=0.6, but protein/mRNA is a deterministic ratio of means, not an independent ribosome-initiation stochasticity measure, so the partial-correlation contrast cannot cleanly separate the two mechanisms.

The degradation rival requires a lon-KO design in the candidate set, but it relies on lon KO uniformly reducing CV; absent a direct per-gene protein half-life measurement, the design cannot distinguish degradation-driven noise from growth-rate/pleiotropy effects of lon KO.

The inverse square-root prediction CV_protein ∝ 1/√mRNA_mean assumes Poisson/birth-death mRNA statistics and no extrinsic noise floor; this critical statistical model is assumed but never stated as a testable premise.
'Transcription burst size' is named in the claim but the operational measure is mean mRNA copy number, which is not burst size; burst size and burst frequency are conflated and unmeasured.

The lon-KO candidate design is included but no decision rule in the primary falsifier uses it; the degradation rival's refuting condition is never operationalized into the reject criteria, so that rival cannot actually fail H1.

Resolving a log-log slope to ±0.1 and R²≥0.7 across only 12 genes spanning mRNA 1–100 requires precise CV estimates; at mRNA~1 copy, CV estimates from 60 seeds have large sampling error that may exceed the slope tolerance.

The question asks what makes any gene's expression noisier, but the hypothesis restricts to constitutive genes with minimal feedback, excluding regulated genes that drive much real expression-noise variation.

Separation of intrinsic vs extrinsic noise is central to the extrinsic-noise rival, but the single-reporter-per-gene design across seeds cannot decompose intrinsic/extrinsic noise (needs dual-reporter), an unstated requirement.
Question asks what makes expression noisier in general, but the hypothesis only tests mean-abundance scaling across 6 genes, ignoring regulatory architecture, operon context, etc.

RIVAL 2's clamped-ppGpp test predicts H1 'persists' and RIVAL 2 'flattens', but H1 itself predicts the slope persists regardless — the result cannot separate 'birth-death noise unaffected' from a null where ppGpp clamp simply does nothing, and ppGpp also changes mean abundances, confounding the regression.

RIVAL 1 and H1 are not mutually exclusive: burst size and mean can co-vary, and matching mean at ~300 while H1 predicts CV~0.06 presupposes the k from the panel fit, so a differing CV could reflect either rival or a poor global fit, not a clean discrimination.

The decision rule has a gap: outcomes with |α|≥0.3 but outside [-0.4,-0.6], or 0.5≤R²<0.7, neither reject H0 nor reject H1, so some results confirm the claim trivially while ambiguous ones are undefined — and a strong negative slope automatically satisfies the rule regardless of whether -0.5 specifically holds.

A 6-point OLS regression yields only 4 residual degrees of freedom; demanding a 95% CI that excludes 0 AND falls in [-0.4,-0.6] AND R²≥0.7 from six gene means is statistically underpowered and fragile.
CV computed from 50 seeds has substantial sampling error that differs per gene; no propagation of per-gene CV uncertainty into the regression, so the R² and slope CI are overstated.

The new_gene perturbation assumes independent tuning of promoter and RBS to hit a target_mean of 300 with controlled burst size; auxiliaries admit the simulator may not support this, leaving RIVAL 1 'formally unresolved' — i.e. the discriminating design may be infeasible.
'Burst size' is invoked as the RIVAL 1 mechanism but never operationally defined or measured; it is only inferred via promoter/RBS labels, so the rival's own causal variable is unmeasured.

Claim labels the panel genes as spanning abundance from 'high' to 'low', yet the panel only includes 'high', 'mid', and 'low-mid' categories with no genuinely low-abundance gene, undercutting the ≥10-fold-range and low-copy birth-death regime central to the claim.

Measurement at a single time point (generation 10) and single point in cell cycle ignores cell-cycle-phase and gene-copy-number (replication) effects that strongly confound protein CV, with no control for aligned cell-cycle stage across seeds.
RIVAL 2's ppGpp clamp design uses ppgpp_conc_multiple=1.0, i.e. clamping to basal level — this imposes no change from wildtype basal, so it cannot reduce CV or discriminate extrinsic noise.

The falsifier requires ≥20 genes spanning mean_mRNA <1 to ≥10, but if the sampled genes are selected to span this range, the slope is quasi-guaranteed by construction; no independent check that selection isn't circular.

RIVAL 1's distinguishing test invokes a new_gene/synthetic high-translation construct, but no such design is in candidate_designs — the three listed designs cannot vary translation rate at fixed mRNA, so RIVAL 1 is untestable.

Separating intrinsic vs extrinsic noise requires dual-reporter or per-gene noise decomposition; auxiliary assumption asserts the engine 'distinguishes' these, but no design measures or exploits this separation.

Low-transcription gene is defined as mean_mRNA<1, yet CV and log(mean_mRNA) regression require meaningful per-gene mRNA; mean<1 implies most cells have zero mRNA, making protein steady-state and CV estimates at generation 3 ill-defined.

The inverse square-root law (CV∝1/√mean_mRNA) actually predicts protein CV from mRNA mean, but protein noise filtering by translation/degradation and dilution is assumed negligible without stated justification.

50 seeds give noisy CV estimates (sampling error in a standard deviation); for genes with mean_mRNA<1 and bursty counts, CV estimates across 50 seeds may be too imprecise to resolve the predicted slope.
'Steady state at generation 3' is asserted but not verified; no criterion given to confirm transient dynamics have relaxed, and 3 generations may not reach steady state for low-abundance proteins.

RIVAL 2's acetate cross-condition test (CV ratios constant) is confounded: H1 also predicts preserved scaling under acetate, so observing preserved ratios does not separate extrinsic dominance from H1.

The question asks broadly 'what makes one gene noisier,' but the design tests only the single transcription-rate scaling law, excluding gene-specific degradation, regulation, and translation determinants that are relegated to untestable rivals.

CV is operationally defined as variability ACROSS seeds (isogenic replicates), yet it is also defined as time-averaged over generation 8 per seed, which collapses within-seed temporal/cell-cycle noise — the two definitions measure different noise sources and are conflated.

The burst-architecture rival's key discriminators (new_gene constitutive construct matched to acrB mean; crp knockout at matched mean) are not in the candidate designs — the Δcrp run exists but no mean-matched comparison is specified, so the rival is not actually distinguished.

The H0-rejection rule accepts any slope in [-0.7,-0.3] with R²≥0.7 as confirming H1, but a birth-death/mean-driven process almost mechanically produces a negative CV-mean slope under repression, so the falsifier is structurally biased toward rejecting H0 regardless of the true noise determinant.

The acrB regression uses only 6 points (5 clamp levels + wildtype), and wildtype/basal ≈ CRP 1.0× basal are near-duplicates, leaving ~5 effective x-values with narrow dynamic range — insufficient power is assumed but not justified for a slope CI test.

The claim invokes 'burst size/frequency' and 'promoter architecture' as noise determinants, but the hypothesis itself concedes burst parameters may not be independently modeled, so the key discriminating mechanism may be unobservable in the simulator.
'Independent of the gene's native promoter architecture' is asserted in the claim but never operationalized as a measurable quantity or tested against a defined contrast.

The question asks what makes expression noisy in general, but the causal test is run on a single gene (acrB) via one regulator (CRP); the cross-gene panel is only correlational, so causal generality is not established.

The extrinsic-noise rival assumes ppgpp_conc clamp at 1.0× isolates ppGpp extrinsic noise, but ribosome_conc and other global fluctuations are left uncontrolled, so a >30% CV reduction (or its absence) cannot be cleanly attributed to ppGpp.

A negative CV∝1/√mean slope is predicted by BOTH H1 and the burst-architecture rival (burst frequency ∝ mean), as the hypothesis admits — so the slope test alone does not discriminate the primary rival, and the proposed tie-breaker designs are absent.

The cross-gene prediction (mean<10→CV>0.5; mean>1000→CV<0.1) is a near-tautological consequence of Poisson counting statistics and would hold under essentially any stochastic model, so it cannot discriminate the causal claim from the null.

Falsifier regresses ribosome_conc on raw fraction_trna_charged (slope CI excludes 0, R2>=0.80), but predicted_effect specifies the slope 1.5-2.0 is on normalized-to-basal values; the two scales are inconsistent and the stated slope band is never actually tested.

The falsifier's acetate-vs-basal arm only requires ribosome_conc to be *lower* in the poor medium (a generic growth effect expected under every rival including passive dilution), so passing it does not confirm the ppGpp/tRNA axis.

The dilution rival predicts ribosome_conc and growth_rate scale proportionally in poor media, which is also broadly consistent with H1's across-media predictions; the five static-media designs cannot separate active repression from passive dilution without the knockout, yet the main falsifier relies only on static media.

The ppgpp_conc '2x clamp' and rrna_operon_knockout are asserted to be mechanistic, but whether the simulator exposes ppGpp as a clampable/held variable (vs. a derived quantity that relaxes back) is never established—if ppGpp cannot be held fixed, the key causal discrimination fails.

The dilution-rival distinguishing result requires ribosome_conc to drop 'more than predicted by dilution alone,' but no quantitative dilution baseline/model is defined, making the discrimination unmeasurable.

Steady-state is assumed reached by generation 8 and all designs run exactly 8 generations, so the no-long-transient/no-oscillation auxiliary is never checked; convergence cannot fail within the design.

Causal claims (clamp decouples, knockout elevates ppGpp) are listed in rivals but the ppgpp clamp and knockout conditions are not wired into the formal falsifier decision rules, so the causal tests are proposed yet not actually adjudicated by any stated threshold.

The question asks how a cell decides ribosome number generally, but the design and falsifier restrict evidence to a narrow carbon-source gradient (acetate/fumarate/malate/succinate) and the single ppGpp pathway, excluding amino-acid/nitrogen media and alternative regulators.

H0 (CV independent of mean) is a near-impossible null for stochastic gene expression; any birth-death system shows some mean-dependence, so rejecting H0 is near-guaranteed and not a discriminating test.

Operational defs and auxiliary assumptions specify 30 seeds, but the 'expression noise' measure states '≥20 seeds per gene'; the stated power claim (<10% CV error) is asserted without justification for genes near the mean>20 boundary.

The burst-size rival predicts deviations from 1/√mean, but the H1 falsifier also rejects on 'slope CI excludes -0.5 OR R²<0.5' — so a burst-driven outcome triggers H1 rejection without identifying burst size as the cause, failing to discriminate the rival from generic scatter.

The extrinsic-noise rival's distinguishing test (clamping ppgpp, pairwise r>0.6) is never incorporated into the decision rule; the main falsifier only fits CV vs mean and cannot separate intrinsic scaling from extrinsic cell-state covariation.

Candidate designs include new_gene and ppgpp_conc perturbations for discrimination, but the formal falsifier/decision rule uses only the wildtype basal regression, so the discriminating experiments are not actually used to reach a decision.

The question asks what makes one gene noisier than another (gene-specific determinants), but the claim reduces noise entirely to mean expression, excluding promoter/RBS/mRNA-stability determinants the rivals invoke.

Assumes the chosen 10 named genes are not confounded by operonic co-regulation or feedback, but no check that they independently sample the mean axis; co-regulated genes would violate the independence assumed by OLS across genes.
Steady-state assumed achieved by generation 8 without any convergence diagnostic; CV estimates conflate transient drift with intrinsic noise if untrue.

'Intrinsic vs extrinsic noise' is invoked in assumptions and rivals but no operational decomposition (e.g., dual-reporter) is defined, leaving the key discriminating construct unmeasurable within the stated channels.
The ppgpp clamp rival predicts a ≥30% uniform CV compression, but no CV-change measurement channel or threshold test is wired into any decision rule, so the prediction cannot be evaluated.

Claim says higher mean mRNA yields HIGHER protein CV (positive β1), but noise theory and the hypothesis's own shot-noise logic predict more molecules = LOWER CV; a positive mRNA exponent alongside a negative protein exponent is physically inconsistent and unexplained.

mean_mRNA and mean_protein are strongly collinear in the promoter sweep (reporters 1-8 vary only promoter at fixed RBS), so the regression cannot cleanly separate β1 from β2, making the ΔR²≥0.2 criterion unreliable rather than a genuine test.
The Poisson-only rival uses overlapping thresholds with H1's own falsifier (both hinge on ΔR²<0.1 vs ≥0.2), leaving a dead zone (0.1≤ΔR²<0.2) where neither H1 confirmed nor Poisson distinguished.

The translation-burst rival's discriminating regression adds log(protein/mRNA) which is exactly log(protein)-log(mRNA), a perfect linear combination of the existing two predictors, so the model is rank-deficient and the term cannot be independently estimated.

Only one RBS-varied reporter and one degradation-tagged reporter are included, providing a single data point each—insufficient to fit the 'matched mean_protein' controls or the degradation-rate covariate the rivals require.

The decision rule treats intrinsic vs extrinsic noise as separable, but across-seed CV conflates both; no procedure (e.g., dual-reporter) is specified to isolate intrinsic noise, yet the claim is about gene-intrinsic amplification.

Burst-size parameters k_on/k_off are stated as not directly observable, yet the mechanism (burst-size-driven amplification) is central; mean mRNA cannot discriminate burst size from mRNA lifetime, as the auxiliaries themselves concede.

The question asks what makes any gene noisier than another, but the design tests only inserted synthetic reporters varying promoter/RBS, not the native regulatory, operon, or feedback features that drive noise differences among real genes.

'Degradation-rate covariate inferred from protein/mRNA ratio and growth rate' is an unvalidated derived quantity with no specified inference procedure or error model, making the rival's test unmeasurable as stated.

Steady-state 'final generation' CV may be contaminated by cell-cycle-phase variance; the auxiliary admits temporal averaging 'may be needed' but the decision rule leaves this unresolved, so the measured CV construct is under-specified.

Decision rule (1) rejects H0 if slope CI 'includes -0.5' but refuting_result rejects H1 if CI 'excludes -0.5' — the acceptance test for the main hypothesis is confirmatory-biased: a slope CI that includes both -0.5 and 0 would pass yet be uninformative.

The burst-architecture falsifier confirms the null-difference (|CV_A-CV_B|<0.05 AND |t|<2); confirming a null via a non-significant t-test with only 50 seeds makes the 'burst irrelevant' conclusion nearly unfalsifiable since low power yields non-significance by default.
CV<0.05 absolute threshold is combined with '(<20% relative difference)' in predicted_effect, but 0.05 absolute and 20% relative are inconsistent for CVs near 0.2–0.3; the two criteria can disagree.

The ppGpp rival's distinguishing design (ppgpp_multiple=1.0 = basal, i.e., no change) cannot clamp or reduce fluctuations; setting the multiple to the basal value is not a clamp and produces no contrast with wildtype.

Claim distinguishes intrinsic from extrinsic noise, but the design measures total protein CV across seeds with no dual-reporter or intrinsic/extrinsic decomposition; the extrinsic 'additive baseline dominated by mean trend' assumption is asserted, not tested or isolated.

The 'new_gene' perturbation is assumed to independently set target_mean_protein=500 AND a specified ≥2-fold burst-size difference via promoter/RBS, but no mechanism verifies the simulator achieves the matched mean or the intended burst ratio; if means differ the matched-mean comparison collapses.

Burst size is defined operationally as translation_rate×mRNA_lifetime yet the hypothesis explicitly declines to measure mRNA, so the '3-fold different burst size' is never directly verified and remains unmeasured.

CV computed across seeds at generation 8 conflates cell-to-cell steady-state variation with cell-cycle/division-stage variance; no gating on division phase, so measured CV may reflect cell-cycle position rather than expression noise.

The question asks what makes expression noisy in general, but the design tests only mean-level Poisson scaling vs. one burst manipulation at a single matched mean (~500), excluding gene-dosage, chromosomal position, regulation, and feedback as noise sources.

Rival 1 (passive growth-law) requires clamping ppGpp to basal in acetate, but the candidate design uses ppgpp_conc multiplier=1.0 which scales endogenous (elevated acetate) ppGpp, not sets it to basal — so the clamp does not produce the distinguishing condition described.

ppgpp_conc perturbation with multiplier=1.0 is a no-op (identity scaling), yet the auxiliary assumption and rival test claim it 'matches basal' — multiplier=1.0 leaves acetate ppGpp unchanged, contradicting the stated causal-direction test.

operational_defs equates 'ribosome abundance decision' with ribosome_conc but auxiliary assumptions worry that ribosome_conc may reflect only engaged/active fraction; the aux note on 'Active ribosome_conc' conflicts with the construct requiring total abundance.

The predicted_effect/falsifier add conjunctive thresholds (|slope|>=0.5, R^2>=0.85, CI excludes 0) with no justification; a true inverse relationship that is nonlinear or shallow would 'refute' H1, making the falsifier reject even when the core claim holds — mismatched to a 'graded, inversely proportional' claim.

The question asks how the cell decides ribosome number (mechanism/sensing), but the design only measures correlations of steady-state ribosome_conc vs ppGpp across 4 carbon sources, never testing the fraction_trna_charged→RelA→ppGpp sensing chain that the claim asserts.

Rival 2 (rRNA operon ceiling) is tested with operons_to_remove=1 and no measurement of fraction-active ribosomes; a single-operon knockout may not produce a detectable 'proportional' shift and the design provides no criterion to separate activity vs total concentration.

No assumption establishes that the four media actually yield distinct, spread-out ppGpp levels; if ppGpp barely differs across basal/acetate/succinate/malate, the regression lacks range to detect any slope regardless of truth.

n=4 conditions for an OLS slope with a 95% CI requirement is only 4 points; the CI/R^2 thresholds are statistically fragile and the regression power is essentially unconstrained by the stated seed count.

falsifier target/reference are set to wildtype/acetate vs wildtype/basal but the decision_rule is a regression across all four conditions — the named pairwise target/reference is unused and inconsistent with the stated rule.
Auxiliary 'quasi-steady-state physiology by generation 8' is asserted without any convergence check or operational test; steady-state is used as a measurement precondition but never verified.

The passive-dilution rival's distinguishing result relies on the SAME ppGpp clamp and relA-KO results the H1 falsifier uses; if the clamp shows <30% effect it simultaneously refutes H1 and confirms the rival, but the design gives no independent read-out separating 'ppGpp causes ribosome change' from 'both track growth rate' — the clamp forces ppGpp exogenously but growth-rate confound is not controlled.

The 2x-basal ppGpp clamp perturbation is run ONLY in basal condition; a clamp that raises ppGpp and lowers growth/ribosomes could reflect generic toxicity rather than the specific feedback, so the falsifier can 'succeed' even if the real mechanism is absent (no clamp-at-fixed-growth or dose-response control).

No stated assumption that clamping ppgpp_conc to 2x holds the variable fixed without directly overwriting the very downstream ribosome-synthesis target it is meant to test — if the simulator implements ppGpp->ribosome as a hard-coded link, the clamp trivially produces the effect, making the test circular.

The rRNA-operon rival predicts ppGpp/tRNA 'unchanged or even elevated' — this disjunction covers nearly all outcomes, so almost any result is consistent with the rival and it cannot be cleanly separated from H1.

fraction_trna_charged is specified as a single scalar, but amino-acid-specific charging varies by tRNA species; measuring one aggregate 'fraction' may not be an available/well-defined simulator observable at the resolution the mechanism requires.

The question asks how a cell 'decides' ribosome number generally, but the design only tests the ppGpp/tRNA-charging axis across 4 media; it cannot adjudicate ribosome regulation mechanisms that are neither ppGpp nor gene-dosage (e.g., direct metabolite or translational-feedback control).

'active ribosome concentration' and 'quasi-steady-state (final 20%)' assume the 4-generation run reaches steady state, but no stationarity criterion is given; if not converged the setpoint measure is ill-defined.

relA-KO is proposed to 'isolate passive vs active regulation,' but E. coli also has SpoT for ppGpp synthesis; deleting only relA does not abolish ppGpp, so a WT-like media pattern in relA-KO cannot confirm passive dilution as claimed.

The quantitative linearity thresholds (slope >=+20 uM/unit, R^2>=0.75 across 4 points) assume a linear ppGpp-ribosome relationship; with only 4 media points R^2 and slope are highly leverage-sensitive and the linearity assumption is unstated.

The falsifier only tests whether acetate ribosome_conc is lower than basal; this is a generic growth-rate correlate that would pass even if the null (growth-rate-only) model were true, so it cannot discriminate H1 from H0/rivals.

Rival 2 (operon dosage) requires a combined operon-knockout + ppGpp-clamp design that the authors themselves state the simulator cannot execute; the proposed indirect substitutes (designs 3 and 4 separately) do not isolate ppGpp's operon-independent effect, so the rival is not actually discriminated.

The predicted_effect and rival 1 both assert the ppGpp clamp in acetate (design absent) restores ribosome_conc, but no design applies ppgpp_conc multiplier 0.1 in acetate — the candidate_designs list only has the clamp in basal (design 5), so the central causal-sufficiency test cannot be run.
The key causal claims (clamp in acetate restoring ribosomes; combined knockout+clamp) rely on perturbations either not present in the design set or explicitly declared unsupported by the simulator.

Assumes 'multiplier 0.1' in acetate yields basal-equivalent absolute ppGpp, but endogenous acetate ppGpp is only predicted to be 3–10 fold above basal, so 0.1× could overshoot below basal; the clamp's absolute target is not verified against a measured basal value.
The ppGpp 'threshold' on tRNA charging and the fraction_trna_charged observable are invoked in H1 but never tested by any design or decision rule, so the charging-threshold mechanism is unmeasured.

The question asks how a cell decides ribosome number in general; the hypothesis restricts the test to a single poor vs rich carbon comparison (acetate vs glucose) and one signaling axis, not addressing nitrogen/amino-acid or other medium-quality decisions.

Design 5 (low-ppGpp clamp in basal, where ppGpp is already low) is predicted to have 'minimal effect' by the authors, making it an uninformative manipulation that cannot distinguish active regulation from passive dilution.
Falsifier decision_rule inverts the t-test logic: 'reject H0 if |t| < 2 (NO significant difference)' — a non-significant result cannot reject the null; this flips rejection and non-rejection.

The acetate-vs-basal channel 'refutes H1' when there is NO significant difference, but the primary claim predicts a difference; as written the falsifier conflates refuting H1 with refuting H0 and cannot cleanly fail against the stated prediction.

The growth-law rival test relies on a ppgpp_conc clamp (2x basal in rich medium), but no rich-medium condition is in the candidate designs — the clamp design is run in basal, so the discriminating comparison cannot be executed.

The ppgpp_conc '2x' clamp assumes the simulator can hold ppGpp fixed independent of tRNA charging/RelA feedback; a mere initial multiplier will relax back under feedback and does not implement a true clamp needed to break causation from correlation.

relA knockout cannot distinguish H1 from the RelA-independent rival because SpoT (also a ppGpp synthetase) may sustain the dose-response; auxiliary assumption admits SpoT contributions, so a residual response is uninterpretable.
Thresholds (slope ranges, R2 >= 0.75, CV >= 15%, 1.5-fold span) are asserted without justification that the five chosen poor-carbon media actually span enough ppGpp/charging range to meet them.
No stated criterion that steady state was actually reached; '4 generations sufficient' is assumed but not verified against the observable (no convergence check on ribosome_conc across generations).

Question asks how a cell 'decides' ribosome number across media generally, but the design restricts to carbon-source variation at steady-state exponential growth, omitting nitrogen/amino-acid-limited and dynamic/shift conditions central to the decision mechanism.

The growth-law rival and H1 both predict the same correlative dose-response across the five wildtype media; only the (unexecutable) clamp distinguishes them, so the primary five-condition regression does not discriminate causation from passive allocation.

The cAMP-CRP rival is tested by the SAME relA/spoT knockout result as H1's own prediction; both the ppGpp-null falsifier and this rival hinge on the identical experiment, so a strong knockout correlation refutes H1 but does not positively identify cAMP-CRP as the mechanism (no cAMP/CRP channel measured).

The claim/h1 center on sensing the fraction of charged tRNA, but the falsifier and decision rule use only ribosome_conc vs growth_rate; fraction_trna_charged and ppgpp_conc are defined as operational constructs yet never appear in any decision rule, so the core sensing mechanism is never actually tested.

The primary falsifier (ribosome_conc rises with growth_rate, R^2>=0.85) is a near-universal empirical regularity in E. coli that both H1 and most rivals predict; passing it does not discriminate the ppGpp-sensing mechanism from passive mass-scaling (H0/rival 1).

The basal-vs-acetate Welch t-test with threshold |t|>=2 and 8 replicates of a deterministic-ish simulator will almost certainly exceed threshold for any mean difference; it is trivially passable and adds no discriminating power.

No stated mechanism or data establish that the four carbon sources actually produce DISTINCT, monotonically ordered growth rates spanning ~0.5-2.0/h; if several media yield similar growth rates the regression collapses, yet this is assumed not demonstrated.

relA/spoT double knockout removes both ppGpp synthesis and hydrolysis; the design assumes this cleanly abolishes ppGpp signaling without lethality or compensatory dysregulation, but no viability/steady-state check across the four media is specified.

The quantitative slope prediction (~40 uM per 1/h, 20 vs 80 uM) and R^2>=0.85 threshold presume the simulator reports absolute active-ribosome concentration in uM calibrated to real values; no evidence the instrument emits comparable absolute units for the knockout/perturbation conditions.

The question asks how a cell DECIDES ribosome number (the sensing/decision mechanism), but the operationalized test reduces to a correlation between ribosome_conc and growth_rate, which measures the output regularity rather than the decision process.

'ribosome production decision' is operationalized merely as steady-state ribosome_conc, conflating the regulatory decision with its downstream level; the decision construct is not independently measurable from a passive-scaling outcome.

Rival 1 (passive mass scaling) is distinguished by ribosome_conc/rna_mass or /cell_mass constancy, but neither rna_mass nor cell_mass is listed as a measured observable in the operational definitions, so the discriminating ratio cannot be computed from the specified channels.

The ppgpp_conc x2.0 perturbation designs (basal, acetate) are included but no decision rule or predicted outcome references them; their role in confirming the ppGpp->rRNA link is left unspecified, making them non-discriminating dead-weight.

Rival 1's distinguishing_result asserts charged-tRNA falls identically in relA KO, but H1/RelA mechanism implies RelA senses uncharged tRNA; this does not discriminate the regulatory program claim and conflicts with the active-response framing.

Rival 1 predicts growth still drops in relA KO (ppGpp near zero), which is also consistent with H1's downstream effects not being the sole cause of arrest; the stated result does not uniquely separate 'passive dilution' from H1.

Falsifier decision rule uses OR between |t|<2 and fold-change<2.0, but with 10 seeds at ~20% CV a 3-fold change yields huge t; the t-test criterion is essentially guaranteed to pass, making the statistical falsifier non-binding.
Falsifier rejects H1 if fold-change < 2.0, but predicted_effect and claim require >=3-fold; a 2.5-fold rise would pass the falsifier yet violate the stated prediction, mismatching thresholds.

Timeline removes amino acids at t=1200 s but the 300-600 s post-shift measurement window and 300 s starvation criteria are referenced relative to shift at t=0; timeline and analysis windows are inconsistent/unexecutable as specified.
Causal relA test assumes SpoT (the second ppGpp synthetase/hydrolase) does not compensate or confound ppGpp levels; no control or assumption addresses SpoT.

The ppgpp_conc clamp at 1.0x rival assumes the simulator can hold ppGpp fixed while perturbing amino acids; feasibility of clamping an internal metabolite is asserted but not established as an available instrument.

Rival 2's distinguishing_result (clamp prevents recovery but not initial drop) is compatible with H1, which does not claim ppGpp causes the immediate arrest; it fails to refute H1 and so does not discriminate.

'amino_acid_shift' is a composite toggle and the model does not track individual amino-acid species, so 'suddenly runs out of amino acids' and uncharged-tRNA sensing cannot be mapped to specific depletion mechanisms.
Assumes amino-acid removal triggers no other starvation signal, but provides no measurement or control to verify carbon/nitrogen/phosphate pathways are not co-activated confounding ppGpp.

Rival 2's distinguishing test relies on ribosome_conc normalizing by cell volume, but the dilution-artifact hypothesis predicts the SAME observable (ppGpp rise, growth arrest); no candidate design measures per-cell ribosome count or ribosome synthesis rate to separate active down-regulation from passive dilution.

The falsifier and Rival 1 both compare against wildtype/basal (no shift), but to isolate the acute starvation response the correct reference for the relA knockout is the knockout's OWN pre-shift baseline; comparing knockout+shift to wildtype/basal conflates knockout basal physiology with the starvation effect (the auxiliary acknowledges this confound but no design resolves it).

Rival 1's discriminating design (relA knockout + shift) cannot distinguish SpoT-mediated synthesis from RelA-mediated synthesis unless the spoT-knockout arm is actually used in the decision rule; the spoT candidate design is listed but never referenced in any distinguishing_result.

The falsifier decision rule requires both |t|>=2 AND fold-change>=3, but with 8+ seeds and an instantaneous total-aa depletion the ppGpp rise is near-guaranteed in any model with RelA, so the falsifier is not a genuine risk of failing; H0 (no response at all) is a strawman that the design cannot realistically confirm.

Operational def assumes >=1 min time-bin resolution on ppgpp_conc, fraction_trna_charged, and growth_rate to capture a 5-10 min transient, but no evidence the simulator exposes sub-generation (<=1 min) summary channels; 'instantaneous specific growth rate in 10 min window' may exceed the instrument's temporal resolution.

Operational def pins the ppGpp window at 5-10 min post-shift while ribosome_conc is measured at 20 min and the timeline runs 3 generations; the 'within minutes'/'5-10 min' claim is inconsistent with the generation-scale (~several hours) simulation windows actually specified.

Auxiliary states the model does not simulate individual amino acid species and operationalizes depletion as a bulk charging shift, yet 'suddenly runs out of amino acids' and instant equilibration of intracellular pools within ~1 min are asserted without a measurable mechanism linking media shift to fraction_trna_charged.

The question asks broadly what a cell does when it runs out of amino acids; the hypothesis measures only ppGpp/growth/ribosome/tRNA-charging and ignores other known responses (e.g., amino acid biosynthesis upregulation, proteolysis, transport induction), answering a narrower stringent-response-only question.

The passive-dilution rival predicts the OPPOSITE sign of ribosome_conc vs growth_rate, but the main hypothesis already predicts monotonic decline with growth rate — so merely observing the declining trend doesn't isolate ppGpp feedback from any active-repression mechanism; the clamp arm, not the media trend, is what discriminates, yet the rival is cast against the trend.

The constitutive/common-upstream rival is tested with relA/spoT knockout in acetate, but its stated 'distinguishing_result' (ribosome rising to match basal) is identical to what the ppGpp-dependence claim predicts, so the described outcome supports both the rival's refutation and the main claim without a clean separating prediction; the rival and H1 are confounded by shared upstream signaling the design cannot separate.

Falsifier clamps ppGpp to 2x basal in BASAL medium and compares to wildtype/basal, but the claim is about growth-rate-dependent equilibrium across media; raising ppGpp in already-rich basal tests only one point and the decision_rule compares target vs the same reference used for the 'rich' endpoint, conflating the perturbation axis with the nutrient axis.

Decision rule rejects H1 if |t|<2 OR reduction <20%, but with n=20 seeds in a deterministic-ish simulator a tiny clamp-induced difference can yield |t|>2 while being biologically trivial; conversely the compound OR with a fixed 20% floor means the falsifier can both reject and the predicted_effect (>=30%) be met — the two thresholds (20% vs 30%) are inconsistent and leave an untested 20-30% gray zone.

fraction_trna_charged is defined as a core observable linking medium to ppGpp, but no candidate design or falsifier measures or perturbs tRNA charging, so the central 'senses tRNA charging' mechanism is asserted but never operationalized or tested.

Auxiliary assumption claims the ppGpp clamp 'faithfully overrides endogenous synthesis/degradation without pleiotropic side-effects,' which is unverifiable within the design and, if false, confounds every clamp result — no control establishes clamp specificity.

'active ribosome concentration' is asserted to reflect the allocation decision while the auxiliary admits the model may not distinguish active vs inactive/sequestered pools — the channel's meaning is thus underdetermined relative to the claim it measures.

The question asks how a cell decides ribosome number 'in a given medium,' but the design tests only carbon-source variation (all respiratory/poor carbons plus basal) with no nitrogen/amino-acid/translation-inhibition conditions, so it probes a narrow slice of nutrient space and generalizes a single-mechanism answer.

Predicted hyperbolic ppGpp-ribosome fit (R^2>=0.85 across >=4 conditions) requires ppgpp_conc to be measured in each wildtype media arm, but it is unstated whether ppGpp is reported per-condition; the fit's feasibility depends on an unlisted measurement channel across the five media.

relA/spoT knockout is assumed to give a complete 'relaxed' (zero ppGpp) phenotype, yet SpoT is the primary ppGpp hydrolase — knocking out both synthesis and hydrolysis has ambiguous net ppGpp effect, undermining the stated assumption that ppGpp synthesis is fully ablated.

H1 requires acetate phase >=30% reduction vs glucose (operational_def says 0.5-0.6 /h), but find_peaks falsifier only requires recovery to >=70% of trough value, which can be satisfied by a second peak far below the 0.5-0.6 /h spec.

Rival 1 (simultaneous co-utilization) predicts a single exponential phase — identical to H0 and to the H1 falsifier's refuting result, so confirming H1 does not uniquely distinguish it from Rival 1 versus H0.

Glucose-glacial diauxie is classically glucose-then-lactose; using acetate (an overflow byproduct secreted during glucose growth) makes the 'two sugars' choice confound secretion/re-import, yet the design assumes acetate behaves as an independent initial substrate without verifying it is not just overflow.

The hypothesis depends on dynamic substrate depletion but admits the instrument reports no extracellular/exchange-flux channels and may run in chemostat mode; the core mechanism (diauxie via depletion) is therefore untestable with available channels.

The question asks how bacteria *choose* between two sugars (mechanism of regulation), but the design only measures growth_rate/dry_mass phenotype and cannot observe the CRP-cAMP regulatory decision; the crp knockout design is listed but never incorporated into any falsifier or rival test.

'10 generations' is used interchangeably as the time axis for growth phases, lag duration (~30-60 min), and find_peaks min_distance, but generation length itself changes between fast/slow phases, making generation-indexed windows (0-3, 6-10) and the minutes-to-generations mapping unmeasurable/ambiguous.

The Welch t-test pools across seeds without defining variance/sample unit; comparing mean growth_rate of two distinct time windows will almost always yield |t|>=2 given large per-timepoint n, so that arm of the falsifier is nearly impossible to fail.

Rival 2's distinguishing test uses the glucose-only control to detect acetate-overflow lag, but overflow acetate accumulation in glucose-only culture is exactly the same process present in the mixture, so a biphasic glucose-only result cannot cleanly separate regulated diauxie from overflow since both coexist.

Claim/H1 treats acetate as the 'secondary sugar' consumed only after glucose depletion, yet acetate is the canonical overflow product E. coli SECRETES during glucose growth — so a positive EX_ac_e during the glucose phase is expected, directly conflicting with the 'near-zero during glucose phase' prediction.

EX_ac_e is a signed exchange flux; secretion (positive) vs uptake (negative) is not disambiguated, so a '3-fold higher' flux ratio could reflect a sign flip rather than increased uptake, making the measure uninterpretable.

Auxiliary assumes acetate is present in 'minimal' medium to support growth post-depletion, but no concentration is specified and the timeline switches to bare 'minimal' — if no acetate is supplied externally the whole falsifier channel is undefined.

Steady-state FBA does not model transcriptional induction lag or enzyme-synthesis kinetics; the predicted 200–600 s induction lag and transient growth-rate dip exceed what an FBA snapshot can produce without an explicit dynamic expression layer.

Auxiliary itself concedes success depends on the simulator capturing cAMP–CRP regulatory coupling and acs/operon dynamics — using acs protein copy-number and tf_activity on Crp presumes a mechanistic regulatory engine FBA alone lacks.

The decision rule's two conditions (≥3× ratio AND |t|≥2) are both plausibly auto-satisfied given deterministic regulatory logic and near-zero glucose-phase baseline (a tiny denominator inflates the ratio), so H0 is nearly guaranteed to be rejected regardless of mechanism.

Rival 2's distinguishing test is a Crp activity clamp, but the candidate design sets activity_multiplier to 3.0 (a modest increase), not a constitutive high/bypass clamp, so it cannot deliver the predicted '≥70% acetate flux during glucose phase' discrimination.

Rival 1 (co-utilization) and H1 both predicted via the same EX_ac_e magnitude thresholds; without separating acetate secretion from uptake, the 'simultaneous co-utilization' signature is confounded with normal overflow metabolism and cannot be told apart from diauxie.

The question asks how bacteria choose between 'two sugars,' but the hypothesis operationalizes only glucose vs acetate (a fermentation product, not a sugar), so it does not address sugar–sugar choice (e.g., glucose vs lactose) as posed.

The wildtype/basal reference arm has no timeline and runs in constant medium, yet the falsifier compares timeline/basal against wildtype/basal without specifying how the static reference's phase intervals [0,1200] vs [1800,3600] are defined for a non-switching run.

Claim lists lacZ, galE, araA, malT, rpoS, recA, lexA, lon, clpP as dispensable, but Rival 1's distinguishing_result calls the biosynthetic genes 'predicted-dispensable' while the claim lists ilvA/serA/cysE/purA/pyrE/thyA as essential — the rival description contradicts the hypothesis's own category assignment.

The falsifier's dispensable list (n=13) includes ptsG, recA, lexA while the claim and predicted_effect assign these to dispensable yet Rival 2 treats ptsG/recA/lexA as redundantly essential; also ptsG/manX/glpK are called 'ambiguous' in the falsifier but ptsG is counted among the 13 dispensable.
Falsifier design lists manX twice ('manX, glpK, manX') as the 3 ambiguous genes, so only 2 distinct ambiguous genes exist; gene counts (13+16+3) are inconsistent with the 32-gene list.

Rival 1 (context-dependent essentiality) predicts biosynthetic genes essential only in acetate; but the main H1 already predicts those genes essential in BOTH conditions, so the acetate-lethal signal does not uniquely separate H1 from Rival 1 unless basal viability is also demonstrated — the design conflates these.

The category-prediction falsifier tolerates ~25% misclassification (<4 of 13, <3 of 16), so a large number of wrong predictions can still pass; combined with broad ±0.10 viable-fraction bands, the falsifier is unlikely to trigger.

Hartigan dip test clause requires p<0.05 in BOTH conditions to 'support' bimodality, but no refuting_result is tied to unimodality — bimodality cannot actually fail the hypothesis, making criterion (iii) non-falsifying.

'growth_rate ~0.4–0.9× wildtype' viable cluster is asserted but the viability threshold (0.1/h) is far below 0.4× wildtype, leaving the intermediate 0.1–0.4× range unclassified and the bimodality claim untestable against the threshold.

Essentiality of genes like recA/lexA/lon/clpP is expected to manifest under stress/DNA-damage, but no stressor is applied in basal/acetate, so the design cannot discriminate their conditional essentiality — an unstated assumption that unstressed growth reveals their dispensability.

Essential-gene knockouts (dnaA, ftsZ, rpoB, secY, groEL) are predicted lethal, yet the protocol measures 'mean growth_rate over generations 2–6' — a lineage that cannot complete generation 2 yields no such measurement, so the instrument cannot produce the specified observable for lethal cases.

The question asks which genes E. coli can live without genome-wide, but the design screens only 32 hand-picked genes while making a genome-wide ≥60% viable-fraction claim, with the representativeness assumption doing all the generalization work.

'non-essential gene fraction ≥60% of screened genes' is computed over a curated, category-balanced 32-gene set, so the fraction is an artifact of gene selection rather than a measurable genome property.
The 5%-of-wildtype viability threshold is so low that almost any non-lethal knockout counts as dispensable, biasing dispensable_fraction upward and making H1 hard to refute on the fraction criterion.

The condition-dependence rival's own 'distinguishing_result' (fraction ~0.30-0.40) lies between H0's <0.20 and H1's >=0.50, so neither H0 nor H1 is rejected and the rival is not actually discriminated by the stated decision rule.

The regulatory-overestimation rival is tested by comparison to external databases (PEC/Keio/DEG), which are outside the simulation's instrument channel and not among the candidate designs, so the simulation cannot discriminate it.
Verifying the simulator against in-vivo essentiality databases (PEC, Keio transposon fitness) exceeds what the whole-cell simulation can output and is not a runnable design.

Functional-class measure lists peripheral-metabolism genes (dnaK, recA, rpoS, acrB, ompC) that are classified as stress/repair, regulation, or transport elsewhere in the falsifier, so the class contrast double-assigns genes inconsistently.
Claim promises genome-wide screen of >=50% of the genome, but the method only samples 100 genes, yet reports a 'genome-wide dispensable_fraction' from that sample.
The question asks which genes E. coli can live without generally, but the test only probes 100 pre-selected genes under two media, not the full genome or diverse conditions.

No stated assumption that the 100-gene sample is representative enough that its dispensable_fraction estimates the true genome-wide fraction; sampling bias toward machinery/essential classes is unaddressed.
Redundancy rival tested only on a single pair {pykA,pykF}; a single negative/positive pair cannot generalize, so the redundancy conclusion is underdetermined regardless of outcome.
'wildtype/basal' is used as the reference denominator even for acetate-condition ratios, conflating two baselines so the acetate dispensability ratio is not measured against a comparable control.
H0 defines bimodality failure as 'unimodal OR flat' but the dip test only distinguishes unimodal from multimodal; a flat distribution is not operationalized, leaving part of H0 untestable.

Question asks generally how bacteria choose between two sugars, but hypothesis fixes on glucose+acetate specifically; acetate is not a sugar, so the model's choice between two actual sugars is never tested.

Both rivals predict UNCHANGED diauxic lag in crp/cyaA knockouts, but the main hypothesis gives no stated prediction for what the knockout does, so the knockout cannot distinguish main claim from either rival.
Rival 1 (stochastic noise) and Rival 2 (metabolic rerouting) both predict knockout-preserved lag, so the knockout designs cannot separate these two rivals from each other.

Claim relies on glucose depletion triggering cAMP-CRP derepression, yet an auxiliary admits the simulator cannot switch carbon source mid-run and relies on 'internal logic' to deplete glucose first — the central mechanism is assumed rather than controlled.

Falsifier and operational defs require per-replicate instantaneous growth_rate sampled every 60s, but whether the whole-cell model outputs smooth instantaneous specific growth rate (vs. noisy stochastic single-cell dry_mass) is never established.
Falsifier requires CV_reference<0.2 confirming monotonic basal growth, but basal is single-carbon and trivially monotonic, guaranteeing that clause passes regardless of the mixed-sugar outcome.

Operational def expects CRP concentration to 'rise during glucose depletion' as a key signal, but no design condition measures or tests CRP dynamics; the CRP observable is declared yet never incorporated into the decision rule.

'Lag duration is 0.5-1.5 generations' and trough windows 'generations 1.5-3' presuppose a known lag timing, but the actual depletion time (tied to GLC[e]<0.1mM) is emergent and may fall outside these hard-coded generation windows.

Rival 1's distinguishing test uses single-cell variability CV>0.5 across seeds, but seeds measure inter-run variation not intrinsic single-cell noise, so the stated observable does not actually discriminate stochastic noise.
Assumes 'minimal_GLC_10mM_AC_10mM' timeline token exists and is parsed as a simultaneous bolus of both substrates, with no verification the simulator recognizes this condition string.

Question asks generally how bacteria choose between two sugars, but glucose and acetate are a sugar vs. an organic acid overflow product, not two sugars; the classic diauxie pair (e.g., glucose-lactose) is the paradigm case being evaded.

Timeline holds glucose fixed at 10mM for the full 3600s (constant concentration), yet the design and falsifier require glucose depletion to trigger the lag/switch — a switch cannot occur if the substrate never depletes.

Acetate is listed both as potential overflow product (secreted during glucose phase) and as the external carbon source at 20mM; the net exchange sign measurement conflates endogenous overflow with uptake, requiring an unstated means to distinguish them.

The three-phase segmentation 'identifies local minima' to define the lag, so a middle phase is found by construction; CV and <0.5x-rate thresholds are then evaluated on a window chosen to minimize rate, biasing the test toward rejection of H0.

The stochastic-noise rival's distinguishing result (crp KO shows no change) is identical in observable terms to the main H1's crp-KO prediction overlap and relies on seed-variability thresholds that the design's 8 seeds may not reliably estimate; it does not cleanly separate deterministic regulation from noise.

cAMP-CRP transcription-factor activity in 'arbitrary units' is asserted as a measured observable (crp_activity) but no candidate design actually reads out TF activity, and whole-cell FBA layers typically do not expose a continuous CRP activity signal.

catabolite_repression operationalized as cAMP-CRP activity in 'arbitrary units' with qualitative low/rising/high bins has no defined scale or threshold, making it unmeasurable for any quantitative decision rule.

The crp-knockout discrimination hinges on CRP-dependent promoters being mechanistically implemented; the hypothesis itself concedes the test may be 'incomplete' if not, leaving the central discriminating control potentially inoperative.

The acetate-only (condition: acetate) control establishes growth-on-acetate capability but no design tests a true two-sugar preference ordering; the 'choice' mechanism is asserted rather than discriminated from simple kinetic preference.

Question/claim frame glucose+acetate as 'two sugars'/diauxie, but acetate is not a sugar and is simultaneously treated as E. coli's own overflow byproduct, confounding the externally supplied vs self-produced acetate narrative.

Rival 2's distinguishing design (exogenous low acetate + glucose) predicts 'diauxic lag' under H1, but the whole premise is that acetate accumulates from glucose overflow regardless, so the manipulation cannot cleanly separate regulatory switch from overflow re-assimilation.

No design implements the Rival 2 discriminators (ackA-pta knockout, lower glucose feed, exogenous constant acetate) nor the cyaA knockout, so the stated rival-distinguishing results cannot actually be produced.

Falsifier uses only growth_rate bimodality and flux non-overlap; since glucose depletion by mass action alone forces sequential uptake and a growth transition, a bimodal/sequential signal is near-guaranteed even under H0/Rival 1, so the test rarely fails for H1.

Predicted_effect conflates 'CV of peak-to-trough ratio ≥ 0.3' with 'trough ≤70% of first peak' — a peak-to-trough ratio is a single number per run, so its CV across seeds is undefined/ill-specified as a within-timeline threshold.

aceB (glyoxylate shunt) is a marker of acetate assimilation, not of cAMP-CRP catabolite repression per se; its rise after glucose depletion is expected under both H1 and Rival 1 (passive kinetics), so it does not discriminate the mechanism.

Rival 1 claims the crp/cyaA knockout would show the SAME diauxic lag if kinetics drive it, but FBA/gene-expression simulators typically model CRP-dependent operon regulation, so removing it will alter uptake regardless of true biology — the predicted 'same lag' outcome is inconsistent with the auxiliary that the simulator faithfully encodes cAMP-CRP.

Resolving a ~30–60 min lag 'over 10 generations' requires sub-generation time-step output for growth_rate, mRNA and flux time-series; sufficient temporal resolution is assumed but not established as available in the instrument.

Rival 1 (bet-hedging) requires single-cell/subpopulation tracking and bimodal lac expression, but aux assumptions state the model does not track single-cell heterogeneity; the proposed bulk channels cannot distinguish bet-hedging (weighted average of two concurrent exponentials) from co-utilization H0.

The timeline hard-codes a switch to lactose-only medium at 3600s regardless of glucose status, so the biphasic transition is imposed by the medium change rather than emerging from glucose depletion/repression as the claim asserts.

Because the timeline forces removal of glucose and provision of lactose-only at a fixed time, a growth-rate trough/transition is manufactured by the design; the falsifier's trough criterion can be satisfied by the medium switch even under co-utilization.

The crp KO is run under the same forced lactose-only-at-3600 timeline, so even if crp KO abolishes active repression, the forced medium change still produces a transition, preventing the KO from cleanly separating Rival 2 (passive kinetics) from H1 (active repression).

Lac operon induction requires an inducer (allolactose/lactose transport) and functional lacI/lacY; it is assumed the model implements lac induction kinetics and inducer exclusion, but these critical regulatory components are never specified.

The in-vivo lag duration of ~10-60 min is cited as the resolution requirement, but no sampling interval is specified and the FBA-style exchange_flux/protein-copy-number instruments may not represent transient induction dynamics at that timescale.
'Catabolite repression strength' is operationalized only as near-zero vs. induced lactose flux, giving no quantitative scale or threshold that maps flux magnitude to a defined repression strength.

CV>0.3 of a growth-rate series that necessarily spans a forced nutrient downshift is nearly guaranteed; the CV criterion adds no discriminating power since any shift from glucose to lactose rates inflates CV.

Rival 2's distinguishing test asserts crp KO 'would have no effect' if Rival 2 is true, but passive-kinetics diauxie could still coincide with crp involvement in lac expression, so the KO outcome does not uniquely separate passive-order from active-repression.

The predicted absolute growth-rate values (0.9-1.0, 0.2-0.3, 0.6-0.7 /h) presuppose specific media/uptake-capacity parameters that are not stated, making the quantitative falsifier thresholds unjustified.

Claim and title frame diauxie as glucose-then-acetate choice between 'two sugars,' but the design hard-codes a timeline that forcibly switches media glucose->acetate at t=1200s, so sequential consumption is imposed, not observed; the cell never 'chooses' between two co-present sugars.

Because the timeline removes glucose and injects acetate at t=1200s, a growth dip and second phase are mechanically guaranteed by the medium switch regardless of catabolite repression, so H0 (monotonic growth) is essentially impossible to realize and H1 cannot genuinely fail.

RIVAL 1 (co-utilization) predicts simultaneous glucose+acetate uptake in the mid-timeline window, but the imposed sequential medium switch prevents both sugars from ever being co-present, so the design cannot discriminate co-utilization from diauxie.

The acetate phase appears in the falsifier channel, but the timeline is the only mechanism delivering acetate; it is never established that observed sequential use reflects endogenous cAMP-CRP repression rather than the forced medium change, and the crp-knockout design result is never incorporated into the decision rule.

RIVAL 2 invokes a relA/spoT double-knockout as an alternative discriminator, but only a ppgpp_conc 0.5x clamp design is listed; the knockout discrimination is asserted without a corresponding candidate design/instrument.

The question asks how bacteria choose between two sugars co-present in one flask, but the hypothesis addresses a glucose->acetate sequential transition (acetate is an overflow product, not a classical second sugar) under a forced switch, not simultaneous dual-sugar choice.

The predicted first-phase growth rate >=0.9 1/h and 1.5-fold peak ratio assume specific absolute growth rates the FBA/whole-cell model produces, with no justification that the model yields these magnitudes; the threshold could pass or fail for reasons unrelated to diauxie.

catabolite_repression_signal is operationalized as cAMP[c] 'rises during glucose depletion' with no quantitative threshold, timing, or decision rule, so it is not actually measured or tested in the falsifier.

Lag duration is predicted at ~30-60 min equated to '0.5-1.0 generations at the acetate growth rate,' but with growth_rate sampled at 10-min intervals the temporal resolution is too coarse to reliably localize a 30-min lag's extrema via a 5-point moving-average derivative.

Question asks how bacteria choose between two sugars 'in the same flask' (simultaneous mixture), but the design uses a sequential glucose-then-acetate timeline and explicitly disavows dual-carbon support — so the test does not instantiate the scenario asked.

Falsifier refuting rule requires growth_rate never dropping below 0.5 /h for >100 s, but a sequential timeline will produce a nutrient-switch depletion trough regardless of regulation, so even H0 cannot yield the stated monotonic refuting result.

Rival 1 (stoichiometric depletion) is tested only with a crp knockout, but in a sequential timeline acetate appears only at t=3600 after glucose is removed, so depletion timing is externally imposed — the design cannot separate regulatory lag from imposed carbon-switch lag.

The sequential timeline guarantees a growth interruption at the glucose-to-acetate switch (glucose removed, acetate introduced), so the trough/bimodality criterion is almost certain to be met for reasons unrelated to catabolite repression — H1's falsifier is nearly unfailable.

No wildtype-vs-knockout baseline matching: the plain 'wildtype' design has an empty timeline (no glucose/acetate), so it cannot serve as the reference for lag-duration comparisons against the knockout timelines.

The claim restricts to the glucose-acetate pair and explicitly excludes generalization, yet the user's question concerns sugar choice generally; the scoped answer leaves 'how bacteria choose' largely unaddressed.

Decision thresholds (trough <0.3 /h for ≥300 s, 5–15 min lag) assume ≤60 s growth_rate sampling resolution; the hypothesis itself flags that coarse-grained reporting would smooth out the trough, so detectability is not established within the instrument.

Rival 2 relies on a ppGpp spike readout, but the auxiliary assumptions never confirm ppgpp_conc and ribosome_conc are observable channels in the design, and these are not listed in any candidate_design's measurement plan.
'Intermediate trough durations (100–200 s) are inconclusive' creates a dead zone that can absorb real outcomes without resolving Rival 1 vs H1, weakening discrimination.

Claim/title frame the question as sugar selection with glucose vs acetate, but acetate is not a sugar and the classic diauxie example (glucose + lactose) is replaced; the 'two sugars' framing is inconsistent with the glucose-acetate pairing used.

Rival 1's distinguishing test asserts crp knockout abolishes the lag while 'ppGpp dynamics remain unchanged' — but if ppGpp transient is downstream of the catabolite switch, crp KO would also alter ppGpp, so the predicted outcome does not cleanly separate the stochastic-tRNA account from catabolite repression.

Rival 2 predicts 'no local minimum and flat ppGpp' — identical to the H0/refuting_result signature, so it is not discriminated from the null rather than from H1; no unique observable separates the FBA-artifact rival from simply falsifying H1.

H0 (constant growth, no lag, no ppGpp transient) is biologically implausible given any carbon depletion, making the alternative trivially favored; the falsifier's refuting_result (CV<10% and no dip whatsoever) sets such an extreme bar it is unlikely to ever trigger.

Decision rule requires detecting a 30-90 min diauxic lag via local minimum, but auxiliary assumptions admit the simulator may not support dual-carbon media or compute exchange fluxes/sugar depletion — the core depletion event may be unobservable in-instrument.

Assumes glucose will actually deplete within the fixed 3600 s / 8-generation window so that a transition is observed, but the glucose starting concentration and uptake rate needed to guarantee mid-run depletion are never specified.

Operational def of lag uses growth_rate <80% of pre-transition mean, but predicted_effect requires a >=40% drop (i.e., <=60%); the 80% threshold and the >=40%-drop threshold define inconsistent lag boundaries.

Sampling instantaneous specific growth rate every 60 s and computing phase-segmented CV/t-tests presumes a smooth, low-noise growth_rate signal; single-cell stochastic simulation output at 60 s resolution may not yield a reliably detectable local minimum.
'Glucose-phase mean' / 'pre-transition mean' baselines are defined circularly via inflection points that themselves depend on detecting the dip, so phase boundaries are not independently measurable.
